result.rationale: The diff visibly replaces the old removal path (`group.remove(user)` in the deleted `update_patch`) with `group.users.delete(user_id)` in `remove_member`. Deleting through a has_many :through association bypasses GroupUser model callbacks/`group.remove`'s bookkeeping, so any counter or cleanup logic there is skipped. Whether user_count is callback-maintained is not verifiable from the diff alone, but the mechanism (bypassing `group.remove`) is real and the spec only asserts `group.users.count == 0`.

judged_text: remove_member replaces the model's removal path (the deleted update_patch used group.remove(user)) with group.users.delete(user_id), which deletes the group_users join rows via a callback-free delete on the has_many :through association, so any bookkeeping the model performs on membership removal (user_count maintenance, GroupUser destroy callbacks) never runs. After every member removal the group's persisted user_count stays inflated (and destroy-callback cleanup is skipped), so the public groups list and the admin pagination show too many members and phantom pages until the count is recomputed; the removal spec only asserts group.users.count == 0 so it cannot catch this.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member the diff changes membership removal from the prior path that called a Group-level API (deleted update_patch used `group.remove(user)`) to `group.users.delete(user_id)`. For a `has_many :through` association, `collection.delete` removes join rows without instantiating/destroying the join model, so any callbacks/counter-cache style bookkeeping on the join model or in `Group#remove` will not run. The diff itself shows the higher-level removal method still exists/was intended (`Discourse.Group#removeMember` calls this controller), but the controller no longer uses a model-level removal hook. The updated spec only asserts `group.users.count == 0`, which would still pass even if cached counts/callback-driven cleanup were skipped.
